source_text: Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις γὰρ λέγει τοῖς παρεστῶσιν αὐτῷ, Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον. Ἰουδαϊκὸν τὸ πλάσμα, τῆς ἐκεῖθεν εὐκολίας τὸ μυθολόγημα· ἵνα τὸν ἕνα μὴ παραδέξωνται, μυρίους εἰσάγουσι. Καὶ τὸν Υἱὸν ἀθετοῦντες, οἰκέταις τὸ τῆς συμβουλίας ἀξίωμα περιάπτουσι· καὶ τοὺς ὁμοδούλους ἡμῶν κυρίους ποιοῦσι τῆς ἡμετέρας δημιουργίας. Τελειούμενος ἄνθρωπος πρὸς τὴν τῶν ἀγγέλων ἀξίαν ἀνάγεται. Ποῖον δὲ δημιούργημα ἴσον δύναται εἶναι τῷ κτίσαντι; Σκόπει δὲ καὶ τὰ ἐφεξῆς, Κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν. Τί λέγεις πρὸς τοῦτο; Μὴ καὶ εἰκὼν μία Θεοῦ καὶ ἀγγέλων; Υἱοῦ μὲν γὰρ καὶ Πατρὸς πᾶσα ἀνάγκη τὴν αὐτὴν εἶναι μορφήν· θεοπρεπῶς δηλονότι τῆς μορφῆς νοουμένης, οὐκ ἐν σχήματι σωματικῷ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ ἰδιώματι τῆς θεότητος. Ἄκουε καὶ σὺ ὁ ἐκ τῆς νέας κατατομῆς, ὁ τὸν Ἰουδαϊσμὸν πρεσβεύων ἐν Χριστιανισμοῦ προσποιήσει. Τίνι λέγει, Κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν; Τίνι ἄλλῳ γε, ἢ τῷ ἀπαυγάσματι τῆς δόξης, καὶ χαρακτῆρι τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν εἰκὼν τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ἀοράτου; Τῇ ἰδίᾳ τοίνυν εἰκόνι τῇ ζώσῃ, τῇ εἰπούσῃ, Ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν, καὶ Ὁ ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ, ἑώρακε τὸν Πατέρα· ταύτῃ λέγει, Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν. Ὅπου μία εἰκὼν, ποῦ τὸ ἀνόμοιον; Καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον. Οὐχὶ, ἐποίησαν. Ἔφυγεν ἐνταῦθα τὸν πληθυσμὸν τῶν προσώπων. Δι' ἐκείνων μὲν τὸν Ἰουδαῖον παιδεύων, διὰ τούτων δὲ τὸν Ἑλληνισμὸν ἀποκλείων, ἀσφαλῶς ἀνέδραμεν ἐπὶ τὴν μονάδα, ἵνα καὶ Υἱὸν νοῇς μετὰ Πατρὸς, καὶ τῆς πολυθεΐας ἐκφύγῃς τὸ ἐπικίνδυνον. Ἐν εἰκόνι Θεοῦ ἐποίησεν αὐτόν. Πάλιν τοῦ συνεργοῦ τὸ πρόσωπον παρεισήγαγεν. Οὐ γὰρ εἶπεν, ἐν εἰκόνι ἑαυτοῦ, ἀλλ', Ἐν εἰκόνι Θεοῦ. Ἐν τίνι μὲν οὖν ἔχει τὸ κατ' εἰκόνα Θεοῦ ὁ ἄνθρωπος, καὶ πῶς μεραλαμβάνει τοῦ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν, ἐν τοῖς ἐφεξῆς, Θεοῦ διδόντος, εἰρήσεται. Νῦν δὲ τοσοῦτον λεγέσθω, ὅτι εἰ μία εἰκὼν, πόθεν σοι ἐπῆλθεν ἀφόρητα δυσσεβεῖν, ἀνόμοιον λέγοντι τὸν Υἱὸν τῷ Πατρί; Ὢ τῆς ἀχαριστίας· ἧς μετέλαβες ὁμοιότητος, ταύτης οὐ μεταδίδως τῷ εὐεργέτῃ; καὶ σαυτῷ μὲν κύρια μένειν τὰ ἐκ τῆς χάριτος παρασχεθέντα νομίζεις, τῷ δὲ Υἱῷ τὴν ἐκ φύσεως ὁμοιότητα πρὸς τὸν γεννήσαντα ἔχειν οὐκ ἐπιτρέπεις; Ἀλλὰ σιωπὴν γὰρ ἡμῖν ἐπιτάσσει λοιπὸν ἡ ἑσπέρα πάλαι πρὸς δυσμὰς τὸν ἥλιον παραπέμψασα. Ἐνταῦθα δὴ οὖν τὸν λόγον καὶ ἡμεῖς κατευνάσωμεν, ἀρκεσθέντες τοῖς εἰρημένοις. Νῦν μὲν οὖν ὅσον διεγεῖραι ὑμῶν τὸν ζῆλον τοῦ λόγου παρηψάμεθα· τὴν δὲ τελειοτέραν περὶ τῶν προκειμένων ἐξέτασιν ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς ἀποδώσομεν, τῇ συνεργίᾳ τοῦ Πνεύματος. Ἄπιτέ μοι χαίροντες, ἡ φιλόχριστος ἐκκλησία, ἀντὶ παντὸς ὄψου πολυτελοῦς καὶ τῶν ποικίλων καρυκευμάτων τῇ μνήμῃ τῶν εἰρημένων τὰς σεμνὰς ὑμῶν κατακοσμοῦντες τραπέζας. Καταισχυνέσθω ὁ ἀνόμοιος, ἐντρεπέσθω ὁ Ἰουδαῖος, ἀγαλλέσθω τοῖς δόγμασι τῆς ἀληθείας ὁ εὐσεβὴς, δοξαζέσθω ὁ Κύριος, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Against Jewish and Anomoian denials of the Son's co-creative dignity
orientation: Basil is closing his exposition of Genesis 1:26, refuting the Jewish evasion that God addressed angels, and the Anomoian denial that the Son shares the Father's image.
pass_a_gloss: For he says to the angels standing beside him, Let us make man. The fabrication is Jewish, the myth-making born of their ease in argument; in order that they may not accept the one, they introduce countless ones. And rejecting the Son, they attach the dignity of counsel to servants; and they make our fellow-slaves lords of our creation. Man being perfected is led up to the dignity of the angels. But what created thing can be equal to the one who created it? Consider also what follows, According to our image. What do you say to this? Is the image of God and of angels also one? For of Son and Father there is every necessity that the form be the same; the form being understood in a way befitting God, clearly, not in bodily shape, but in the peculiar character of the divinity. Hear also you, the one from the new mutilation, the one who promotes Judaism under the pretense of Christianity. To whom does he say, According to our image? To whom else, indeed, than to the radiance of his glory, and the exact impress of his substance, who is the image of the invisible God? To his own living image, therefore, to the one who said, I and the Father are one, and, The one who has seen me has seen the Father; to this one he says, Let us make man according to our image. Where there is one image, where is the dissimilarity? And God made the man. Not, they made. He fled here from the plurality of persons. Through those words instructing the Jew, and through these words shutting out Hellenism, he safely ran back up to the monad, in order that you may understand the Son with the Father, and may flee the danger of polytheism. In the image of God he made him. Again he introduced the person of the co-worker. For he did not say, in his own image, but, In the image of God. In what respect then man has the being according to the image of God, and how he receives a share of the being according to the likeness, in what follows, God granting, it will be said. But now let this much be said, that if there is one image, from where did it come upon you to commit unbearable impiety, saying that the Son is unlike the Father? O the ingratitude; of what likeness you received a share, this you do not grant to your benefactor? And for yourself you consider that the things supplied from grace remain secure, but to the Son you do not permit the likeness by nature toward the one who begot him to be held? But silence now commands us, since evening long ago sent the sun on its way to its setting. Here then let us also put the discourse to rest, being satisfied with what has been said. Now then we have touched upon as much as would awaken your zeal for the discourse; but the more complete examination of the matters set before us we will render in what follows, with the cooperation of the Spirit. Go from me rejoicing, O Christ-loving church, instead of every costly dish and the varied seasonings, adorning your august tables with the memory of what has been said. Let the one who says unlike be put to shame, let the Jew be turned to shame, let the pious one rejoice in the doctrines of the truth, let the Lord be glorified, to whom be the glory and the might unto the ages of ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: put to rest, lull to sleep

choices.english: the myth-making born of their ease in argument
choices.why: εὐκολία means facility or ease, here the readiness with which the Jews multiply persons rather than accept the one; 'ease in argument' preserves the polemical force without importing 'laxity'.
rejected: the myth-making born of their laxity
the easy fabrication from that source

choices.english: the one from the new mutilation
choices.why: κατατομή is Paul's polemical term for circumcision (Philippians 3:2); 'mutilation' keeps the insulting force Basil intends against Judaizing Christians.
rejected: the one from the new circumcision
the one of the new cutting

choices.english: the exact impress of his substance
choices.why: Echoes Hebrews 1:3; 'exact impress' renders χαρακτήρ as the stamped image, and 'substance' keeps ὑπόστασις distinct from οὐσία.

choices.english: he safely ran back up to the monad
choices.why: ἀνατρέχω means to run back or up; Basil pictures Moses retreating from plurality to the unity of God, and 'monad' preserves the philosophical term.
rejected: he securely returned to the unity
he safely ascended to the one

choices.why: ἀφόρητα is adverbial accusative plural, 'unbearably'; rendering as 'commit unbearable impiety' keeps the force of the accusation against the Anomoians.

choices.term: τῇ μνήμῃ τῶν εἰρημένων τὰς σεμνὰς ὑμῶν κατακοσμοῦντες τραπέζας
choices.english: adorning your august tables with the memory of what has been said
choices.why: κατακοσμέω means to adorn or decorate; the image is of the congregation taking the sermon home to ornament their dinner tables, contrasting with costly food.
rejected: decorating your solemn tables with the remembrance of the words
furnishing your venerable tables with the memory of the sayings

pass_b_english: For they say he is speaking to the angels who stand beside him: 'Let us make man.' The fabrication is Jewish, the myth-making born of their ease in argument. So that they may not accept the one, they introduce countless persons. And rejecting the Son, they attach the dignity of counsel to servants, and make our fellow slaves lords of our creation. A man who is being perfected is raised up to the dignity of angels. But what created thing can be equal to its creator? Consider also what follows: 'According to our image.' What do you say to this? Is there one image of God and of angels? For of the Son and the Father there is every necessity that the form be the same—the form being understood, of course, in a way befitting God, not in bodily shape, but in the distinctive character of the Godhead. Hear also, you who are from the new mutilation, you who promote Judaism under the pretense of Christianity. To whom does he say, 'According to our image'? To whom else but the radiance of his glory and the exact impress of his substance, who is the image of the invisible God (Colossians 1:15)? To his own living image, then, to the one who said, 'I and the Father are one' (John 10:30), and 'Whoever has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9)—to this one he says, 'Let us make man according to our image' (Genesis 1:26). Where there is one image, where is the dissimilarity? 'And God made the man' (Genesis 1:27). He did not say, 'They made.' Here he fled from the plurality of persons. Through those words he instructs the Jew, and through these he shuts out Hellenism, and he safely ran back up to the monad, so that you may understand the Son with the Father, and may escape the danger of polytheism. 'In the image of God he made him' (Genesis 1:27). Again he introduced the person of the co-worker. For he did not say, 'In his own image,' but, 'In the image of God.' In what respect, then, man has that which is according to the image of God, and how he receives a share of that which is according to the likeness, will be said in what follows, God granting it. But for now let this much be said: if there is one image, where did you get the idea to commit unbearable impiety, saying that the Son is unlike the Father? O the ingratitude! The likeness you received, this you do not share with your benefactor? And you think that the things granted to you by grace remain yours by right, but you do not permit the Son to have the likeness to the one who begot him that is his by nature? But the evening now commands us to silence, having long ago sent the sun toward its setting. Here, then, let us also put the word to rest, content with what has been said. For now we have touched upon the matter only enough to awaken your zeal for the word; but we will give a more complete examination of the things before us in what follows, with the cooperation of the Spirit. Go in joy, O Christ-loving church, adorning your august tables with the memory of what has been said instead of every costly dish and varied seasoning. Let the one who says the Son is unlike be put to shame; let the Jew be confounded; let the pious rejoice in the doctrines of the truth; let the Lord be glorified, to whom be glory and might forever and ever. Amen.

last_rejected.why: 'εὐκολία' means 'ease'/'facility' in a negative sense of 'laxity' or 'looseness,' not skill in argument; 'their ease in argument' misrepresents the charge.

last_rejected.ruling: εὐκολία means 'ease/facility'; 'ease in argument' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: you who are from the new mutilation
last_rejected.why: 'κατατομή' is a polemical term for circumcision, playing on 'περιτομή'; 'new mutilation' misses that this refers to circumcision and its typological 'new' form.
last_rejected.ruling: κατατομή means 'mutilation' (vs περιτομή); 'new mutilation' captures the polemical circumcision wordplay adequately.

last_rejected.quote: he safely ran back up to the monad
last_rejected.why: Subject is ambiguous in Greek but context suggests God/the text as subject; 'he' is unclear and awkward. 'Monad' is obscure for modern readers.
last_rejected.fix: safely he returned to the unity
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνέδραμεν ἐπὶ τὴν μονάδα: 'he safely ran back up to the monad' is within normal rendering; 'monad' is the source term.

last_rejected.quote: Let the one who says the Son is unlike be put to shame
last_rejected.why: 'ὁ ἀνόμοιος' is a technical term for the heretic who holds the Son is 'unlike' (ἀνόμοιος) the Father—an Anomoean; 'the one who says the Son is unlike' over-explains and loses the technical force.
last_rejected.fix: Let the Anomoean be put to shame
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ ἀνόμοιος rendered as 'the one who says the Son is unlike' preserves meaning; technical force is a preference, not error.
